newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana crowned Trivial Pursuit Queen.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana crowned Trivial Pursuit Queen.

text.p: Princess Diana was crowned Queen of Trivial Pursuit on Tuesday -- she was the subject of a record 27 questions in the internationally popular board game.
Reflecting Britons' insatiable appetite for royal gossip, she topped the question chart in the 1997 edition ahead of Queen Elizabeth who tied for second place with the Duchess of York.

Diana's former husband, heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles, slumped to fourth place. He had long been the prime source of fascination for people playing the game that was invented by three Canadian journalists who are now multi-millionaires.
"Charles has finally been toppled by Diana. She is now the queen of trivia. She leads such a trivial lifestyle," said question composer Brian Highley.

"When I go down to the pub in the evening, I find it is the Royals that fascinate people most," he said at the launch of the latest British edition. "I don't think the questions will offend anyone," he said.
Avid royal watchers are asked what colour blouse Diana wore for a controversial television interview and challenged to pick the nationality of the stalker who compulsively followed her.
